lastPrompt: This is a Java data-structures course project with two parts: six lab experiments (`Experiments/`) and fifteen homework assignments (`Homework/`). Most core algorithm functions have been stubbed out with `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("TODO: implement")` and you must restore their implementations so that the project compiles and all tests pass. Your working directory is `/workspace`. The full source tree is already present under `/workspace/Experiments/` and `/workspace/Homework/`. Implement the following modules: Run the following experiments: DSExp01_Stack (`Experiments/DSExp01_Stack/`): Stack-based infix/postfix expression processing. Converts infix expressions (with +, -, *, /, ^, parentheses, and variable symbols) to postfix notation, tokenises expression strings, inserts implicit multiplication for variable terms, and evaluates postfix expressions numerically. Reads from `samples.txt`. (~2 files, ~4 functions to implement) DSExp02_Tree (`Experiments/DSExp02_Tree/`): Binary-tree construction and traversal. Builds a binary tree from user input, supports recursive and iterative pre-order/in-order/post-order traversals, level-order traversal, tree-property classification (full/complete/balanced), and lowest-common-ancestor queries. (~1 file, ~13 functions to implement) DSExp03_Graph (`Experiments/DSExp03_Graph/`): Graph construction and traversal on both adjacency-matrix and adjacency-list representations. Builds structures from an edge-list data file, converts between representations, and performs recursive/iterative DFS and BFS from every vertex. Reads from `data.txt`. (~1 file, ~15 functions to implement) DSExp04_Search (`Experiments/DSExp04_Search/`): Binary-search-tree operations and binary-search analysis. Builds BSTs from ordered and random data files, supports insertion, deletion (with delete-min), search, and in-order sort. Also builds a half-search (decision-tree) structure for sorted arrays, and computes average successful/unsuccessful search lengths for both BST and half-search. Reads from `order.txt` and `random.txt`. (~1 file, ~21 functions to implement) DSExp05_Hash (`Experiments/DSExp05_Hash/`): Consistent hashing with virtual nodes. Generates server IP addresses, maps them onto a hash ring using a hash function (FNV-like), supports adding/removing servers and looking up which server handles a given key. (~1 file, ~7 functions to implement) DSExp05_RedBlackTree (`Experiments/DSExp05_RedBlackTree/`): Red-black tree with full insert/delete/rebalance. Builds a red-black tree from `order.txt`, supports left/right rotations, post-insert and post-delete rebalancing, search, in-order traversal, and average search-length analysis. (~1 file, ~13 functions to implement) Homework: DS01 (`Homework/DS01/`): Four standalone programs — custom-comparator quicksort for string arrays, two-pointer maximum-finding in arrays, DFS-based Hamiltonian-path search on a graph, and a sports-competition scoring/query system with file serialisation. (~4 files, ~14 functions to implement) DS02_LinkedList (`Homework/DS02_LinkedList/`): Product inventory management via a sorted linked list. Supports adding, deleting, searching (by name/brand), updating, and file-based persistence. (~1 file, ~11 functions to implement) DS02_Matrix (`Homework/DS02_Matrix/`): Sparse-matrix transposition using triple (row, col, value) representation. Implements both a naive O(cols*n) transposition and a fast O(n) transposition with pre-computed column counts and start positions. (~2 files, ~5 functions to implement) DS02_String (`Homework/DS02_String/`): Pattern-matching on a linked-list representation of strings. Constructs a character-level linked list from input and performs substring matching against it. (~1 file, ~2 functions to implement) DS03_Huffman (`Homework/DS03_Huffman/`): Huffman-coding file compression and decompression. Reads a text file, computes character frequencies, builds a Huffman tree, encodes content to a binary file with a key f
